title: WordPress: the named lines of a template part (the footer's copyright) are written in the site's one language, identity tokens kept
steps: S1: No stand and no site. From the TCH checkout run: node --test --test-name-pattern="named lines of its parts|loses an identity token" apps/tracy-web/test/brief-wordpress.test.mjs

S2: The WordPress brief engine runs against a fake site whose footer part is the one JA Essence WP 1.0.10 stores (fixture ja-essence-wp7-1.0.10-footer.html): once in Vietnamese, once in Vietnamese with an answer that drops {site.title}, once in English.
S3: Read the node:test summary lines (tests / pass / fail) and every failing test name.
expect:
Vietnamese site: footer.copyright reads the planner's two Vietnamese runs around the
, {year} and {site.title} kept, the block keeps metadata.name footer.copyright.
An answer without {site.title} is not written; English site: the line is not planned and keeps the template words.

selectors.seam: judging / sweepWordPress in apps/tracy-web/src/sites/brief-engines/wordpress.js and wp-residue.js (namedRuns, editRuns in wp-leaves.js)
selectors.door: the line planner (fake model in the tests); content.update of the template part

evidence: Dev (cowork.tracy.site), 10/10/2026: g56-ess-wp-full (JA Essence WP 1.0.10, Vietnamese) printed 'All Rights Reserved. WordPress is Free Software released under the GNU General Public License.' in the footer of every page (LANG-2).
fence: Unit tests with a fake site and a fake model over the real 1.0.10 footer part; no live WordPress site and no model ran. Dev sites made before the deploy keep their words.

cmd: --test-name-pattern=named lines of its parts|loses an identity token
